newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down sharply on technicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down sharply on technicals.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Monday in a moderate session, pressured the entire day by deteriorating technicals and mild weather forecasts for much of the nation, sources said.
Spot-July skidded 12.9 cents to close at $2.11 per million British thermal units. August settled 11.3 cents lower at $2.129. Other months ended down by one-half to 9.6 cents.

"Technically, it doesn't look good, and there's still no (hot) weather. Odds favor a lower open tomorrow," said one Midwest trader. But he said he expected good end-user buying in the low-$2s (basis July).

While traders agreed mild weather patterns over much of he nation and forecasts for more of the same next week could keep cash and paper on the defensive for a while, most expected the first signs of summer-like heat to send the bears for cover.

Chart traders agreed the technical picture turned negative Friday after July's close below trendline support. They said today's follow-through and weak close made more liquidation a likely scenario near-term.
"I think we washed a lot of the length out, but we could see another day or two of selling before the industrials and utilities step in (to buy)," a trader said.
Support in July was first seen in the $2.085-2.095 area, with further buying likely near $2.05. Resistance was seen at $2.21, $2.25, $2.37-2.38 and the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, Gulf Coast swing prices slipped four cents Monday to the $2.14-2.19 area. Midcon pipes were off a couple of cents to the low-$2s. New York city gate gas was talked little changed in the mid-$2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip tumbled 5.7 cents to $2.20. NYMEX said 48,161 contracts traded, almost double Friday's revised tally of 24,868.

On the KCBT, July finished 11.9 cents lower at $1.985, while deferreds ended down by two to 11 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 12.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 134 lots traded, down from Friday's total of 314.
